The <ruby>Yoshino Style Rules of Engagement<rt>Yoshino Onryu Kassen Reiho</rt></ruby> is a martial art for warriors. In the age when every head of the senior Minato house was himself a warrior, the art went down to one heir only, together with the sword-armor.

Then the Minato clan stepped out of the warrior register, and almost at the same time the art also was thrown away. After that, custom was that a man of the Minato household inherits it: either the husband of the priestess-princess, or a son who cannot become the priestess-princess.

Being an art of warriors, naturally its methods reach completion in mounted combat in sword-armor, the battle in the sky, flower of the warrior. But that is not <ruby>all<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby> it has. Do not think so.

At the foundation stage the Yoshino style divides broadly into three systems: swimming, unarmed movement, and armored swordsmanship. When a student has learned all three, he is allowed to study sword-armor operation, which is the integration of the three. After that, full license.

If you ask by training hours, sword-armor operation actually gets the smallest share. This is seen in <ruby>combat arts<rt>rules of engagement</rt></ruby> of warriors in general and is not strange at all. The Yoshino style is not a widely known school, but its technique inside is very <ruby>standard<rt>orthodox</rt></ruby>.

The reason for this tendency is, I think, the difficulty of combat training in sword-armor. These days mass-produced suits are available, so group training of warriors is common sense in the army. Earlier, one suit per household was normal.

So the ideal teaching, a warrior holding another warrior's hand and showing step by step, was very rare. Meaning, the experienced man could not give direct practical teaching to the inexperienced one.

In another discipline, this arrangement might be fatal to the teaching. One boat available. One person fits inside. Kindly teach the novice to sail it. The practical difficulties, and the <ruby>time and trouble<rt>time and trouble</rt></ruby> involved, may be imagined.

But if you open the old records of the warrior schools, it was not considered such a big problem.

Of course, teaching did fail sometimes. A man learned the foundation completely, then donned sword-armor and could not fly properly, and never got his license in the end... Such people also existed, it seems.

<ruby>吉野御流合戦礼法<rt>よしのおんりゅうかっせんれいほう</rt></ruby>は武者の為の武術である。
　かつて皆斗本家の歴代当主が武者であった時代には、
劒冑と共にこの戦技も一子相伝されたと云う。

　が、皆斗家が士籍から離れると、ほぼ同時期にこの
武術も捨てられ、以後は湊斗家の男――巫姫の婿又は
巫姫たり得ない男児――が継承する慣わしとなった。

　武者の術であるから当然、その技法は劒冑を用いて
の騎航戦闘――武者の華たる空の戦いにおいて完成を
見る。
　といって、<ruby>それだけ<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>ということもない。

　吉野御流は基礎段階においては泳法、体術、そして
甲冑刀法の三系に大別される。
　これらすべてを習得すると、三系の統合に基く劒冑
操法を許され、皆伝免許となる。

　鍛錬の比重を問えばむしろ劒冑操法が最も少ない。
　これは武者<ruby>戦斗術<rt>れいほう</rt></ruby>の全般に見られる傾向で、珍しい
話では全くなかった。吉野御流は広く知られた流派で
こそないが、技法の内実はごく<ruby>標準的<rt>オーソドックス</rt></ruby>なものである。

　こうした傾向になる理由は、劒冑を用いた戦闘訓練
というものの難しさ――数打劒冑が量産される現在で
こそ武者の集団訓練は軍の常識となったが、かつては
一家に一領が普通であった――がそれであろう。

　武者が武者を手取り足取りに教えるという、理想的
な教育形態はごく珍しいものだった。
　それはつまり、経験者が未経験者に対して直接的な
実践教育を施せないということを意味する。

　他の技術であれば、これは致命的な問題ともなった
であろう。一隻しかない船の操法を素人に教える――
しかもその舟はごく小型で一人しか乗れないとなった
ら、果たしてどれほどの<ruby>手間隙<rt>てまひま</rt></ruby>が必要となることか？

　しかし武者武芸諸派の過去の記録を紐解くと、そこ
までの問題とはされていなかった事がわかる。

　無論、教授の失敗が無かったわけではなく。
　基礎を完全に習得しながら、劒冑を装甲すると満足
に飛ぶこともできず、遂に免許を得られなかった……
そういう者もいたらしい。

en.text:
But these stories are very few.

One who has absorbed the foundation sufficiently, even without practical coaching from a sword-armor user, generally learns sword-armor operation, the art of fighting in the sky, without much suffering. Such is the completeness of the foundation course.

In unarmed training you learn the basic movement of the body.
In swimming you learn movement not on a flat plane, but in space.
In armored swordsmanship you learn how to fight with armor on.

And the one who integrates it all, even doing armored combat training underwater, will hardly be confused when he acquires sword-armor and jumps into the sky. Speed is different, yes, but the feeling is more or less the same.

............Or so.

Well. As common belief, that is what is supposed to happen.

Naturally, I have never worn sword-armor. How close this widely accepted martial wisdom comes to the truth—or how far it misses—I am not qualified to say. Nor am I likely to acquire that qualification in my lifetime.

To begin with, the Minato house is not a warrior lineage, so keeping or operating sword-armor is not legally permitted for us. Practical experience was never going to happen.

Inheritance of the Yoshino style finishes after the three foundation arts, with a ceremonial handing-over of secret teachings that suppose sword-armor use. To call this a warrior's martial arttechnique might even be called arrogance. ...But that I did not care about at all.

The family Rules of Engagement include, as basic training, arts that do not use sword-armor. ◆For me now, only that part has any meaning.

だがそういった話はごく稀だ。

　基礎を充分に身につけた者は、劒冑使用経験者から
実践指導を受けられずとも、大概さほどの困苦はなく
劒冑の操法を――空で戦う術を心得る。
　つまりは基礎課程の完成度がそれだけ高いのである。

　体術訓練において基本的な運体を学び、
　泳法において平面的ではなく空間的な運動を学び、
　甲冑刀法において装甲状態での戦い方を学ぶ。

　そしてその統合として、水中での着甲戦闘訓練まで
こなした者は、劒冑を得て空へ躍り出てもまず戸惑う
ことがない。
　速度差はあるにしても、感覚的にはほぼ同じなのだ。

　…………と。
　
　まあ、通念としてそういう事になっている。

　無論俺は劒冑を纏った経験など無いので、広く知ら
れているこの武術的常識がどの程度真実に近いのか、
また離れているのか、何も語れる立場にない。
　生涯そうだろう。

　そもそも湊斗家は武者の家系ではないから、劒冑の
所持運用を法的に許されない。
　実用経験など積むべくもなかった。

　吉野御流の継承は基礎三技術を習得後、形式として
劒冑使用を想定した秘伝の伝授を行い、完了する。
　これで武者の武術わざを称するなど、あるいは不遜とも
言えたろう。……が、そんな事はどうでも良かった。

　家伝の合戦礼法が、基礎修練として劒冑を用いない
武術も含んでいる――◆今の俺にとって意味があるのは、
そちらの方だ。

The most basic practice swing. It is training for the cut from the high guard, the correct position in <ruby>sword combat<rt>tachiuchi</rt></ruby>.

In competitive kendo with bamboo swords, and in the unarmored sword arts that are its <ruby>foundation<rt>base</rt></ruby>, "high guard" mostly means the sword lifted big over the head. But in warrior swordsmanship, this right-shoulder carry is the high guard.

The reason is simple: put the sword over your head, and the helmet objects. A stroke delivered while carefully avoiding its horns is hardly going to break another warrior's steel.

Not stepping is also because of conditions special to warriors. If you step, meaning shift body weight, the force of the stroke increases by a jump. This is certain.

But that is on the ground.

In the sky, the <ruby>force<rt>energy</rt></ruby> of weight shift comes from high-speed flight, made by the output of the <ruby>Gattari<rt>barrel</rt></ruby>, the precision of the <ruby>wing armor<rt>wing</rt></ruby> and the <ruby>altitude advantage<rt>high position</rt></ruby>. Footwork has no turn there.

What a warrior should train on the ground is therefore a power usable in the sky also: arm strength and the <ruby>spring<rt>spring</rt></ruby> of the upper body.
So the practice swing takes this form.

最も基本的な素振りだ。
　<ruby>太刀打<rt>タチウチ</rt></ruby>における正位、上段構からの斬りつけを想定
した鍛錬にあたる。

　竹刀を用いた競技剣道、あるいはその<ruby>基盤<rt>ベース</rt></ruby>となった
素肌剣術においては、上段といえば剣を頭上へ大きく
振りかぶった構を指すことが多い。
　が、武者剣法においてはこの右肩担ぎが上段である。

　理由は単純な事で、頭上へ振りかぶると兜が邪魔に
なるからだ。
　腕が兜の角に引っ掛からないよう注意しつつの上段
では、到底、武者の甲鉄を打ち破る剣など望めない。

　足の踏み込みを行わないのもまた、武者特有の条件
を踏まえての事であった。
　足の踏み込み……つまりは体重移動を行えば、剣撃
の威力は飛躍的に増す。これは、間違いない。

　だが、地上での話だ。
　空における体重移動の<ruby>力<rt>エネルギー</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>合当理<rt>バレル</rt></ruby>の出力と<ruby>母衣<rt>ウイング</rt></ruby>の
精度、そして<ruby>高度優勢<rt>ハイ・ポジション</rt></ruby>によって成し得る高速騎航から
生み出されるもの。足技の出番は無い。

　武者が地上において鍛えるべきは、空の打ち合いに
おいても活用可能な力――即ち腕力と上半身の<ruby>撥条<rt>バネ</rt></ruby>で
あった。
　従って、素振りはこの形になる。

Lift with the inhale, cut down with the exhale. The upper body contracts in step with it. When lifting, the chest swells forward; when cutting down, it shrinks in toward the spine.

This is, strictly, practice for sword combat in the sky. But does it mean nothing in a fight on the ground? Not necessarily.

Often a master of unarmored swordsmanship will say strength is not needed to handle a sword, and laugh at the force-based sword method of warriors. And true, the subtlety of sword arts specialized for unarmored ground fighting is far beyond anything in a warrior's sword work.

There are plenty of stories: a warrior famous as unmatched in the sky meets a sword-expert grandfather on the ground, no sword-armor allowed, and gets thrashed with one <ruby>stick of firewood<rt>stick of firewood</rt></ruby>. But those stories are strictly at master level.

This time I swing with a step. Arm strength, back and chest strength, and the force of weight shift on top.

Just before the point of the wooden sword touches the earth floor, the squeeze of my hands stops the cut. From the feel I know: with this much striking power, even if the opponent held a weapon of the same weight and blocked firmly, I would most likely push through.

Letting a blow miss by a hair's breadth, or skillfully deflecting tremendous force to subdue an opponent: such things happen only in a master's wonderland or in an amateur's daydream. Not so easy as people say. In a match with an ordinary opponent, it will almost never come up.

The warrior's sword is generally power-based, but <ruby>force<rt>force</rt></ruby> is the simplest kind of <ruby>strength<rt>・・</rt></ruby>. Simple, so easy to understand and easy to use. The <ruby>technique<rt>technique</rt></ruby> of unarmored swordsmanship is complicated. Perfected, it may be invincible, but that is difficult, and it does not come out without mind and body both full.

Seeing both as a kind of tool, you could say they differ in <ruby>ease of use<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>. Which is superior cannot be compared so simply.

Also, even if not as intricate as the unarmored arts, warrior swordsmanship has many <ruby>techniques<rt>techniques</rt></ruby> of its own. Most of them can be applied to ground fighting.

"A dragon that <ruby>soars through heaven<rt>soars</rt></ruby> loses its <ruby>sword-armor<rt>wings</rt></ruby> and becomes a <ruby>earth-dragon<rt>mole</rt></ruby>." People who dislike warriors often say this famous line. That it points to the truth correctly, I could not think.

...Family partiality may be speaking. A non-warrior has little use for warrior swordsmanship. Perhaps I should have studied an unarmored style instead. A reasonable conclusion. Only, accepting it is rather painful.

I cannot roll time back and change my choice. And even if I could, carrying the Minato family art was a duty laid on me, so nothing can be done.

The Yoshino style was the only martial road permitted to me. To conclude that the road went nowhere would not be especially healthy for my state of mind.

............But.
Even if I put my own emotional problem to one side, something still remains.

今度は踏み込みと共に、一振りする。
　腕力、背胸筋力、そこへ体重移動の力が乗る。

締めが運剣を止めた。その手応えで把握する……

　尋常の敵手との立会いでは、まず無い事態だろう。

<ruby>強さ<rt>・・</rt></ruby>だ。単純ゆえに理解し易く、使い易い。
　素肌剣術の<ruby>技<rt>ワザ</rt></ruby>は複雑だ。極めれば無敵であろうが、
それは難しく、また心身の充実なくして発揮されない。

　一種の道具として見て、<ruby>利便性<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>に差があると言って
も良いだろう。
　簡単には優劣を比較できない。

　それに、素肌剣術ほど複雑巧緻ではなくとも、武者
刀法とて数々の<ruby>術技<rt>わざ</rt></ruby>を有する。
　その多くは地上戦への応用が可能なものだ。

　<ruby>天翔<rt>あまか</rt></ruby>ける竜、<ruby>劒冑<rt>はね</rt></ruby>を失くして<ruby>土竜<rt>もぐら</rt></ruby>となる――武者を
嫌う者がよく口にするかの名句が正しく事実を指した
ものだとは、俺には思われなかった。

　実際のところ、武者ではない俺が武者刀法を修める
意味は少なく、素肌剣術をやっていれば良かったのだ
ろうが、そうと認めてしまうのはなかなかに辛い。

　時間を過去へ巻き戻して選択を変えられるわけでは
ないし、仮に変えられるとしても、湊斗の家芸を継ぐ
のは俺に課せられた責務だったのだからどうにも仕様
がない。

　吉野御流だけが俺に許された武芸の道なら、それを
無意味なものとは思いたくなかった。
　心理的健康のために宜しくない。

　…………だが。
　単なる俺の感情的問題を脇へ除けても、まだ、残る
ものはある。

I admitted it inwardly. Even if I attacked suddenly from where I stood, she would block it without effort. It was only a few years since I began teaching Hikaru the Yoshino style... and already her ability had passed mine.

No, it was like that from the first. When Hikaru asked to train in the Yoshino style, the senior house refused permission, because it went against custom. So Hikaru started stealing my techniques <ruby>without permission<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>.

<ruby>Three days later<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>, she asked me for a match and beat me. My talent is ordinary, yes, but even so, only "abnormal" fits her gift.

With the fact already made, she forced the senior house to approve, and began proper training. About two years. At a speed without precedent, Hikaru reached the doorstep of the inner license.

Truth is, I have taught almost nothing. A girl who watched my training from a hidden corner for three days and went beyond my skill: her growth was exactly "hear one, know ten".

Maybe for that reason, I hardly feel master-and-disciple towards her. Even "the blue is better than the indigo" feels complicated. Rather than a <ruby>kite<rt>kite</rt></ruby> giving birth to a hawk, it is more correct to say a hawk happened to take lodging in a kite's house.

I feel proud, yes, but not as a master who guided his student. More as the brother of a genius sister. In the birth of that genius, I cannot find anything I did.

Still... this one thing, at the very end, I must teach as her master. Not technique; it belongs to the discipline of the heart.

Hikaru's back blurred.

An instantaneous step.
The cut down—

Her weapon, a battlefield sword with a <ruby>clamshell edge<rt>clamshell edge</rt></ruby>.
The target, a steel suit of armor and helmet.

　　　　　　　　　　　　Helmet Splitter

心中で、認めておく――今ここから不意に攻め掛か
ったとしても、苦も無く防がれるであろうと。
　光に吉野御流の手解きを始めてまだ数年……しかし、
実力は既に俺を凌いでいた。

　いや、それは最初からそうか。
　そもそも光が吉野御流の修行を希望した時、慣例に
反することだとして本家の許諾を得られなかったのだ
が――すると光は<ruby>勝手に<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>俺の技を盗み始め、

　<ruby>三日後<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>には俺に立合いを求めて打ち負かした。
　俺の凡才もあるが、それにしても異様な資質という
他はない。

　そうやって事実を先行させる形で強引に本家の承認
を得、正式に修練を開始して二年ばかり。
　前例の無い速度で、光は奥伝免許の手前まで至って
いた。

　実のところ、俺が教えた事など皆無に近い。
　物陰から三日間、俺の修行風景を眺めただけで俺の
技量を超えた光だ。その成長ぶりはまさに一を聞いて
十を知るというものだった。

　その為か、どうも光に対して師弟という意識が薄い。
　出藍の誉、と考えるにも複雑だ。<ruby>鳶<rt>とんび</rt></ruby>が鷹を生んだと
いうよりも、鷹がたまたま鳶のもとに居候したと表現
する方が適切に思える。

　誇らしくは感じるのだが、それはどちらかと言えば
弟子を導いた師としてではなく、天才の妹を持った兄
としての心情だった。
　天才の誕生において、己が何を為したとも思えない。

　しかし……最後に、この一つだけは、師として教え
ねばならないだろう。
　それは技術ではなく、心法に属する事柄であるが。

　光の後姿が霞んだ。

　瞬速の踏み込み。
　打ち下ろし――

　得物は<ruby>蛤刃<rt>はまぐりば</rt></ruby>の戦場太刀。
　据物は鉄の鎧兜。

　
　　　　　　　　　　　　兜割

I had meant it as a joke. Hikaru did not come along. She just lowered her face and thought. ...The joke being poor cannot be the only reason. She did not have her usual ease.

My chest hurt. It is the rule of the school, there is no help for it, but still it is almost like cheating my sister.

This Helmet Splitter is the last trial for anyone who wants the license of the Yoshino style. The student is given a heavy, thick-edged sword and told to cut a suit of armor and helmet <ruby>entirely in two<rt>・・</rt></ruby>.

But, from the very ground up, this is impossible. Armor and helmets are <ruby>made so that they cannot be cut<rt>・・・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>.

Many masters and experts in the past challenged this divine feat. Some of them succeeded.

But even those did not cut anything in two. Take the most famous and most recent example, Kenkichi Sakakibara's Helmet Splitter before the Emperor: a gash slightly more than three sun across was made in the helmet, and that was counted as success.

That is what helmet splitting is, originally. That much cut is enough; it would be fatal to the person inside, and even a sword saint's art cannot go deeper than that.

Cutting in two is not needed, and is not something a human can do. <ruby>And moreover<rt>Moreover</rt></ruby>: where Kenkichi Sakakibara and others tried on ordinary armor, the final test of the Yoshino style uses a <ruby>dead sword-armor<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>.

The remains of a suit of sword-armor that a head of the senior Minato house once rode as his favorite. As sword-armor it is already dead and its supernormal power is gone, but the toughness of its steel is still in good health. If a tank drove over it, not even a dent.

A blow of a sword from a living human body cannot possibly split it.
Impossible.

<ruby>Impossible<rt>・・</rt></ruby>, I say.
This last trial orders you to do what cannot be done.

Hikaru admitted it in a strangely empty voice.

Does the word "father" stir nothing in her... or does she not know what she should feel? Either way, it was painful.

Hikaru's father, my foster mother's husband, my foster father, is not at present in the Minato household. In place, and also in law.

Soon after Hikaru was born, my foster father, who often differed in opinion with the senior house, was driven out and had his name removed from the Minato register. Now he has gone back to his old surname and holds a public post in Kamakura.

For the senior house, once a successor to the Minato priestess-princess was there, there was no reason to keep an eyesore of a man nearby. To that person, a man of the Minato house is only breeding stock.

So Hikaru had never met her father. They must have seen each other right after her birth, but surely there is no memory.

Even after my foster father left the house, I sometimes went to Kamakura and met him, but Hikaru had no such chance. The senior house never looks kindly on the priestess-princess daughter leaving this land.

My foster father, from his side, also does not come near here. Busyness is one reason. ...Another may be that he thinks more of the people who would not welcome him than of the people who would.

But—

　だが――
